zh.CATEGORY: 建站工具 / AI 设计代理（Website Builders）
zh.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: 它卖的不是 AI，是「设计稿直接变成能上线的站」：画布即生产环境，AI 只是把这一步再压短。
zh.USER_SCALE: 可核实：Marketplace 收录 28,915 个资源（模板 / 组件 / 插件 / 矢量）；定价页写 99.99% uptime；官网客户位置引用 Miro、Perplexity、Zapier、FLORA、Metalab、Cradle 的口述证言。第三方站点转述：G2 4.5 分（约 142 条）、Trustpilot 约 1.6 分（约 127–140 条，其中 74% 为一星）。官方未披露 ARR、站点数、付费用户数——本卡不编。
zh.STAGE_MATURITY: 成熟期。官网叙事已整体切到 design agent（导航三项挂 New：AI / Agents / External Agents），产品面覆盖 Agents、CMS、Hosting、Analytics、SEO、AEO、Convert、Localization、Marketplace、Hire Experts。公司成立年份与融资情况本次采集页未披露，不写 [推断] 以外的内容。
zh.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: 按站点订阅（Free / Basic / Pro / Enterprise）+ 席位（编辑器 HK$81/月、内容编辑 HK$41/月）+ 附加包（语言包 HK$81/个、Convert A/B 测试 HK$203/50 万事件、Advanced hosting HK$811）。本次抓到的金额为港币区域价（见 _raw.md），美元价为第三方评测转述，不作官方口径。
zh.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: 它把「设计稿直接变成能上线的站」卖成了订阅，AI 只是加速器；真正的护城河是编辑器手感＋托管＋模板市场，真正的伤口是按站点、按人头、按用量叠起来的账单。
zh.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: 作为「AI 嵌入型」产品，拔掉 AI 它仍然是可用的建站工具（实测拔电测试结论：嵌入）。所以它的门槛不在模型，在软件本身——SEO 能力、托管、以及设计师已经养成的操作习惯。评论区分裂得很清楚：G2 夸的是编辑器，Trustpilot 骂的是账单与支持，这两件事同时为真。
zh.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: AI 是加速器，不是产品本体
zh.TLDR_1_BODY: 官网把 Agent 放在第一屏：描述需求 → 生成布局与组件 → 在画布上改 → 一键发布。但实测（燃冰）走完一圈的结论是：AI 替掉的是「从零搭骨架」这一段，审美判断仍由人做。拔掉 AI，产品还在。
zh.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: 真正的门槛是软件，不是模型
zh.TLDR_2_BODY: 实测（燃冰）原话：门槛在产品本身的 SEO，以及设计用户的习惯，在软件。托管、CMS、AEO、Core Web Vitals、99.99% uptime 这些是模型给不了的，也是竞品最难一次补齐的。
zh.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: 账单是它最脆的一根梁
zh.TLDR_3_BODY: 首页不提一个价格，定价页却叠了三层：站点订阅 + 席位（HK$81/编辑器）+ 附加包（语言、A/B、Advanced hosting）。Trustpilot 约 1.6 分、74% 一星，抱怨集中在计费与取消，而不是设计能力——这就是「营销面干净 / 账单面复杂」的代价。
zh.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: Framer 是一个把设计、CMS、托管、分析、SEO 合成一条线的网站构建平台：你在画布上设计的东西就是最终上线的页面，AI 设计代理负责按描述生成布局、组件与代码片段。
zh.USER_PROMISE: 官网原话：Framer is the pro website builder with a world-class design agent；以及 Build your website with agents and make it your own on a fully editable design canvas。翻译成用户语言：不用交接给开发，设计完就能发。
zh.SEGMENT_1_NAME: 设计师与设计驱动的市场团队
zh.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: 官网 Solutions 直接列 Designers / Agencies / Marketers / Growth / Builders / Engineers / Site Teams / Founders；客户证言全部由设计负责人出镜（Miro 设计负责人、Perplexity 设计负责人）。他们要的是「设计权在自己手里」——评论原话：design ownership back in our hands。
zh.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: Free 档就能建、买域名才付费（定价页：连接自定义域名需升级），对项目周期拖延的 freelancer 是真金白银的缓冲。实测（燃冰）的判断也是这一层：免费用户也有很好的价值，比如模板和社区。
zh.SEGMENT_3_NAME: 代理商与企业站点团队
zh.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: Enterprise 档给 SSO、SCIM、uptime 保障、无限编辑器；定价页另写 Pro Experts 对客户项目有免费编辑权限，r/framer 里官方人员提到 agency programme。但按站点计费叠席位，正是这类用户抱怨最集中的地方。
zh.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: 把一个设计想法（截图、参考站、Figma 稿）变成能对外发布、能被搜索引擎抓到的真站点，不经过开发交接。
zh.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: 不想再等排期、不想再为一个 padding 改三封邮件，也不想被人看出「这个站是模板拼的」。
zh.JTBD_SOCIAL: 对外看起来有一个完整的品牌站点——客户证言里反复出现的词是 ship updates daily、no dev handoff。
zh.TRIGGER_MOMENT: 要上新品牌站 / 改版落地页 / 赶一场发布会，而设计稿已经定了、开发还没排进来。
zh.FREQUENCY: 项目制：改版与上新时高强度，平时低频维护（[推断] 依据：定价按站点与带宽计费，不是按对话次数计费）。
zh.USAGE_CONTEXT: 浏览器为主（官网另列 Desktop App）；发布后由 Framer 托管（99.99% uptime），内容进 CMS，数据看内置 Analytics，实验走 Convert 附加包。
zh.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: 触发点不是「我想用 AI」，而是「这一步现在卡在别人手里」。评论与实测指向同一个场景：手上有成品设计，需要它变成站。
zh.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: 描述需求 / 导入设计，在画布上改
zh.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: 官网给的三步：Describe what you need（agent 生成布局与高级组件）→ Refine on the canvas（字号、组件、断点、特效全可改）→ Publish complete sites instantly（托管、CMS、分析、SEO、AEO 已在）。
zh.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: 一个能直接发出去的站
zh.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: 奖励不是「生成了一段代码」，是「域名绑好就能上线」。实测（燃冰）判定：能直接用，改的是每个组件细节，且支持直接对外发布。
zh.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: 站点是活的：活动页、A/B 实验、多语言、CMS 上新都会把人拉回画布。循环的黏性来自资产沉淀在它这里（站点＋CMS＋分析），不来自 AI 的惊艳。
zh.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: 高频出现在「改版那一周」，而不是每天；这也是它把计费做成订阅而不是按次的原因——按次收不到维护期的钱。
zh.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: 它教用户的是「不用等开发」这件事本身；一旦团队习惯了设计即上线，再回到交接流程就会觉得慢——这是它最真实、也最容易被账单抵消的留存。
zh.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: 三条公开路径：① Marketplace 28,915 个资源做长尾入口（模板页本身就是 SEO 页）；② 官网大量 compare 页（vs Webflow / Figma / Wix / Squarespace / WordPress / Lovable / v0 / Claude Code…）截「选型意图」流量；③ 客户证言与作品展示做社会证明（Miro、Perplexity、Zapier 等设计负责人出镜）。
zh.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: 实测（燃冰）：把一张真实设计稿/截图做成能上线的页面，且 AI 能按需求换部件——原来要几个月的事，几小时完成。啊哈点不在「它写得像人」，在「它直接产出了可以发布的东西」。
zh.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: 弱且是副作用：站点页脚有 Made in Framer 一类的归属，作品展示与模板作者会带来自然扩散，但产品内没有邀请机制、没有协作裂变。它靠作品传播，不靠关系链传播。
zh.RETENTION_1: 资产锁定：站点、CMS 内容、分析数据都在它这里，且官方不提供代码导出（评论与第三方评测一致点名），迁移等于重建。
zh.RETENTION_2: 习惯锁定：设计师已经把断点、组件、Scroll 动效的操作路径练熟；换工具的代价是重新学一套肌肉记忆（实测（燃冰）：门槛在设计用户的习惯，在软件）。
zh.RETENTION_3: 生态锁定：模板、组件、插件、Experts 市场把「找个人帮我改」也留在了平台内。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_1_NAME: 模板与作品 → 搜索与社区 → 试用
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: 28,915 个 Marketpace 资源每一个都是一张落地页；模板作者为了卖模板主动做外链与教程，平台不付流量费。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_2_NAME: 对比页截流 → 迁移 → 反哺口碑
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: [推断] 官网为几乎每个竞品都建了 compare 页，这是长尾 SEO 的标准吃法：用户在「选哪个」这一刻被接住。第三方评测也印证了迁移路径存在（有用户从 Webflow 迁入且称四个月 SEO 无损失）。
zh.SURFACE_1_ROLE: 产品本体。左侧 Pages / Layers / Assets，右侧属性面板，顶部断点与 Publish——设计对象就是生产对象。
zh.SURFACE_2_ROLE: 描述需求生成布局/组件/文案，也能生成代码与图片；官网演示里它会先给「design plan」再动手。
zh.SURFACE_3_ROLE: Collections / Fields / Plugins 三层，内容与画布联动；Free 档 10 个集合、1,000 页，付费档按集合数与条目数分档。
zh.SURFACE_4_ROLE: 标题、URL、描述、社交预览图、语言包比例、分支与发布；技术 SEO 的天花板就在这一页（评论点名 robots.txt 与静态文件受限）。
zh.SURFACE_5_ROLE: 内置访客、页面浏览、跳出率、平均时长，加 A/B 变体与转化率；Convert 是附加包，按事件计费（HK$203/50 万事件）。
zh.SURFACE_6_ROLE: 28,915 个模板、组件、插件、矢量；找不到人还能直接在平台内找专家，把服务也留在生态里。
zh.ENTITY_1: Site / Project（一个站点，计费单位）
zh.ENTITY_2: Page / Breakpoint（页面与响应式断点）
zh.ENTITY_5: Locale / Branch（语言版本与发布分支）
zh.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: 主轴是「站点」而不是「文件」：先选项目，再选页面，再选断点与图层；CMS、分析、SEO、语言都是站点下的子配置。它没有「知识库」这一层，资产就是站点本身——这也是迁移成本高的结构原因。
zh.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: 对设计师几乎零学习成本（Figma 式画布），对非设计师有一个词汇门槛：Breakpoint、Collection、Branch、Locale、Credits 这些词要先学会。实测（燃冰）没有卡在界面上，卡在「审美判断」这一步——界面不难，判断难。
zh.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: 没有「设计稿 → 交付 → 重建」这一段：你在画布上改的就是上线的那一版。这是它所有体验优势的根，也是所有锁定风险的根。
zh.CRAFT_2_NAME: AI 生成 + 全可编辑
zh.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: 官网原话 Everything stays editable；生成的不是一张图，而是一组可拆的图层与组件。评论里被夸的也是这一点：生成后能逐件改，而不是重画。
zh.CRAFT_3_NAME: 把 SEO / AEO / 性能做成默认值
zh.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: 首页直接摆 Core Web Vitals 实测面板（LCP 1.1s / INP 95ms / CLS 0.01），并有 AEO scanner、Stack Score 这类自家工具。卖点不是「能优化」，是「默认就好」。
zh.CRAFT_4_NAME: 三层计量：站点 + 席位 + credits
zh.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: credits 供 Agent / 本地化等 AI 功能消耗，全工作区共享；超出可加购。这套设计让重度使用能持续变现，也让账单变得难预测（Trustpilot 抱怨的主要来源）。
zh.CRAFT_5_NAME: 用对比页把选型流量收干净
zh.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: 导航 Compare 下列了近 20 个对手（Webflow、Figma、Wix、Squarespace、WordPress、Lovable、v0、Claude Code、ChatGPT、Replit、Astro…）。每一页都在回答同一个问题：为什么不是它。
zh.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: 先让设计师愿意在里面待着，再谈 AI 能生成多少。它所有 AI 功能都长在画布上，而不是另开一个聊天窗口——这是它和「一句话生成站」类产品的根本差别。
zh.TTV_LABEL: 价值到达时间：本次未测（实测只记「几小时完成一次页面替换」，未做计时）
zh.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: 实测（燃冰）记录的是量级不是秒表：原来几个月的事，几小时。本报告不把「几小时」写成精确值，也不把未计时的环节写成数字。
zh.COG_LABEL: 认知负荷：中（设计师低，非设计师中高；词汇门槛在 Breakpoint / Collection / Locale / Credits）
zh.DELIGHT_1: 生成之后所有东西都能改（官网原话 Everything stays editable，实测（燃冰）也是「改每个组件细节」而不是重做）。
zh.DELIGHT_2: MCP 对外开放：Claude、Codex、Cursor 都能接进来改文案、导 CMS 内容（官网原文 Connect your AI with MCP，端点 mcp.framer.com/mcp）。
zh.DELIGHT_3: 默认性能面板就摆在首页：LCP 1.1s、INP 95ms、CLS 0.01——把「快」当成可展示的事实而不是形容词。
zh.DELIGHT_LABEL: 惊喜点：全可编辑的生成 + MCP 外接 + 默认性能
zh.TRUST_LABEL: 信任：产品层有 uptime 承诺（99.99%）与 Enterprise 的 SSO/SCIM；信任事件集中在计费（credits 自动加购、席位、附加包）与支持响应（第三方转述：机器人优先、答复慢）。
zh.STRUGGLE_1: 账单不可预测：站点订阅 + 席位 + credits + 附加包四层叠加，第三方转述的 Trustpilot 差评主要集中在「升级/加购超出预期」。
zh.STRUGGLE_2: 没有代码导出，迁移等于重建：评论原话（转述）impossible to leave framer without export and they do not provide it。
zh.STRUGGLE_3: 技术 SEO 有天花板：第三方转述指出无法编辑 robots.txt、静态文件上传被锁在 Advanced hosting 附加包后。
zh.STRUGGLE_LABEL: 摩擦：账单不可预测、无法导出、技术 SEO 受限
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: 订阅（按站点）+ 席位 + 附加包
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: 定价页四档：Free（500 credits、Framer 子域名、1 GB 带宽）/ Basic（1,000–15,000 credits、自定义域名、2 个 CMS 集合、50 GB）/ Pro（3,000–100,000 credits、10 个集合、100 GB、重定向、Staging、分支预览，A/B 与 Advanced hosting 为加购）/ Enterprise（自定义额度、SSO、SCIM、无限编辑器、uptime 保障）。退款：EU 与土耳其 14 天。
zh.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: 免费档可以建、可以预览，但定价页写明「连接自定义域名需要升级」——付费扳机不是 AI 用完，是「要上线」。这一刀切得很准：项目没上线前不收费。
zh.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: Free：500 AI credits/月、Framer 子域名、1 GB 带宽、10 个 CMS 集合、1,000 页、5 MB 单文件上传、1 个免费语言、最多 3 位协作编辑；不能绑自定义域名。超限规则：带宽可超一个月并邮件提醒升级；credits 不够可加购或升级站点。
zh.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: 局部一致、整体打架。一致的地方：付费点（域名）正好是价值点（上线），用户不会觉得被卡。打架的地方：credits 与席位是「用得越多付得越多」，而它的体验目标是「让你一直改」——改得越多，账单越不可预测，这就是信任分的裂缝。
zh.COMP_1_D1: 设计师向的专业建站（同一批人）
zh.COMP_1_D2: 自研可视化 CSS 引擎 + 托管，导出与代码控制更强
zh.COMP_1_D3: 代理商与专业建站社区
zh.COMP_1_D4: 有公开定价页；金额本次未逐个核实
zh.COMP_2_D1: 通用建站（同一段需求，不同人群）
zh.COMP_2_D2: 模板 + 拖拽 + 全托管，AI 生成站为附加能力
zh.COMP_2_D4: 有公开定价页；金额本次未逐个核实
zh.COMP_3_D2: 设计工具内直出站点，省掉「导入建站工具」这一步
zh.COMP_3_D3: 已有设计团队的默认位
zh.COMP_3_D4: 随 Figma 订阅；本次未核实
zh.COMP_4_D1: 一句话/一段提示生成站（AI 侧夹击）
zh.COMP_4_D2: LLM 生成 React/Tailwind 代码 + 第三方部署，可导出源码
zh.COMP_4_D3: 开发者与 AI 尝鲜者渠道
zh.COMP_OWN_D1: 设计即上线的专业建站 + 一站式托管
zh.COMP_OWN_D2: 画布即生产环境、AI 生成全可编辑、CMS/分析/SEO/AEO 内置
zh.COMP_OWN_D3: 设计师社区 + 28,915 资源市场 + 大量对比页截流 + MCP 外接
zh.COMP_OWN_D4: 首页零价格，定价页四档 + 三层附加；港币区域价已抓到
zh.COMP_INTRO: 名单来源：官网 Compare 页自己列的对手（Webflow、Figma、Wix、Squarespace、WordPress、Readymag、Ceros、Unbounce、Lovable、Claude Code、ChatGPT、Codex、Contentful、Sanity、AEM、Replit、Astro、v0）+ 第三方评论里用户实际提到换去的地方。Product Hunt 的 Similar Products 本次未取到（页面被 Cloudflare 拦），已注明。
zh.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: 设计与发布的连续性：同一块画布上完成「想—做—发」，且生成物可逐件修改。评论里被反复夸的是断点调整与动效成本（同一处改动不用重做），这是壳层产品（LLM 生成代码）目前给不了的手感。
zh.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: 三条：① 要代码主权的人被 LLM 生成类（Lovable / v0 / Claude Code）截走，因为它们能导出源码；② 内容与电商复杂度的上限被 Webflow / Shopify 压住（评论点名 CMS 上限、无原生电商）；③ 免费与低价的边缘被 Wix / Squarespace 与开源方案吃掉。
zh.CHANNEL_1: 模板与作品生态：Marketplace 28,915 个资源做长尾入口，模板页本身就是落地页。
zh.CHANNEL_2: 选型对比页：官网 Compare 下近 20 个竞品页，接住「到底用哪个」的搜索意图。
zh.CHANNEL_3: 客户证言与 Experts 市场：Miro / Perplexity / Zapier 等设计负责人口述 + 平台内找专家，把服务也留在生态内。
zh.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: 站点订阅 + 席位（HK$81/编辑器）+ credits + 附加包（语言 HK$81/个、Convert HK$203/50 万事件、Advanced hosting HK$811）四层叠加。第三方站点转述的 Trustpilot 差评（约 1.6 分、74% 一星）主要集中在「自动升级/加购超出预期」。用户不是不愿付，是付之前算不出来。
zh.FRICTION_2_TITLE: 没有代码导出，走了就重建
zh.FRICTION_2_BODY: 评论转述原话：impossible to leave framer without export and they do not provide it；r/framer 的共识是 lockin and lack of code export are the trade-offs for that simplicity。它是商业选择，也是信任成本。
zh.FRICTION_3_TITLE: 技术 SEO 的天花板说不清
zh.FRICTION_3_BODY: 第三方转述：无法编辑 robots.txt；静态文件上传（最多 500 个）锁在 Advanced hosting 附加包（HK$811）。官网卖点是 Built-in SEO 与 AEO scanner——元标签与结构化没问题，再往下要先查清能力边界再决定把站交给它。
zh.FRICTION_4_TITLE: 支持响应是第二条差评线
zh.FRICTION_4_BODY: 第三方转述：支持机器人优先、答复慢，Trustpilot 上有「不回复负评」的标记；Capterra 的易用性子分也是全项最低。对一人公司伤害最大——出问题时没人可问。
zh.METRICS_INTRO: 官方未公开任何运营指标。以下是可核实事实 + [推断]，用来说明「它该看什么」，不代表真实数据。
zh.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: 已发布站点数 × 每站点月活维护动作（[推断]）
zh.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [推断] 它按站点订阅、按席位与 credits 增收：站点数是收入底座，「还在改」是续费与加购的前提。所以它要的不是注册数，是「站上线且一直有人动」。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_NAME: 免费档 → 绑定自定义域名的转化率
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: 这是它唯一的付费扳机（定价页写明绑域名需升级）。这个数字决定免费档是成本还是漏斗。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: 每站点 credits 消耗与加购率
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: credits 是 AI 功能的计量单位，也是账单争议的来源；加购率高说明 AI 真在干活，同时说明抱怨会跟着涨。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: Pro 档席位（编辑器）附加率
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: 席位是第二增长曲线，也是最容易被吐槽的一项（HK$81/编辑器）；它决定「团队版」能不能撑起来。
zh.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: 计费/退款投诉数 + 支持首响时长
zh.GUARDRAIL_WHY: Trustpilot 的低分与 G2 的高分同时存在，说明产品满意度不等于商业满意度；这两条是唯一能把「设计口碑」和「账单口碑」分开监控的护栏。
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: 没有公开留存曲线、迁移率、毛利率，也没有「每站点带宽/推理成本」口径 [推断]
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [推断] 它卖订阅、付带宽与推理：只看收入不看单位成本，越增长越难看的毛利会被藏起来；而「无法导出」会同时压低迁移率、抬高投诉率，两个方向都不透明。
zh.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: 编辑器手感 7、托管/CMS/SEO 一体化 7、模板生态 7、迁移锁定 8、价格与支持 4、AI 能力 5，加权 6：抄得动的是 AI，抄不动的是「设计即上线」这套耦合。
zh.HORIZONTAL_1: 从建站扩到运营：Analytics、Convert（A/B、漏斗）、Localization、SEO/AEO scanner——把「上线之后」也吃掉。
zh.HORIZONTAL_2: [推断] 从设计师扩到市场与创始人：Solutions 已按 Designers / Marketers / Founders / Agencies 分入口，话术从「设计工具」转向「增长工具」。
zh.VERTICAL_1: 专业站点与品牌站：作品集、落地页、营销站、代理商客户站（Pro Experts 对客户项目有免费编辑权限）。
zh.VERTICAL_2: CMS 驱动的内容站：Blog、Case、活动页；上限在集合数与条目数（Pro 加购后最多 40 个集合、40,000 条）。
zh.PLATFORM_1: 有开放接口：MCP 端点 mcp.framer.com/mcp 让 Claude / Codex / Cursor 等外部 agent 直接改站点内容，发布前在画布复核。
zh.PLATFORM_2: [推断] 平台化走「协议 + 市场」：不靠抽成交易，靠 MCP 把外接 agent 变成免费劳动力，靠 Marketplace 把模板作者变成免费渠道。
zh.OPP_1_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把「改完即上线」做成可核对的差异清单
zh.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: How：每次 Agent 改动后给一份「动了哪些图层/组件/文案」的清单，一键回滚到上一版。Why：实测（燃冰）说改的是每个组件细节，而审阅能力决定人敢不敢放手让它改；这也是它相对「一句话生成站」唯一能守住的信任差。
zh.OPP_2_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把示例驱动做成内置的参考库
zh.OPP_2_DETAIL: How：Agent 首轮就要求「给一个你想像的示例」，并把需求写成结构化 brief 让人确认，再动手。Why：实测（燃冰）明确写「它要求我找示例、给需求」，而这一步正是审美判断的门槛——产品把它接住，非设计师才进得来。
zh.OPP_3_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把账单做成开工前的预算
zh.OPP_3_DETAIL: How：动手前显示这次改版会消耗多少 credits、涉及哪些附加包（语言/A/B/托管），超限前预警。Why：Trustpilot 约 1.6 分的主因是账单不可预测，而这项改造不需要架构变动，是最轻的一刀。
zh.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: 赌注：用 AI 降低「从零到可上线」的门槛，用托管与生态把站留住
zh.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: 它同时押两件事：一是把 Agent 做成画布的一部分（设计代理、CMS 代理、代码代理），让非设计师也能开工；二是继续把上线之后的事（托管、分析、A/B、多语言、AEO）收进订阅。第一条扩人群，第二条提 ARPU——中间那个「无法导出」是它敢这么押的底气，也是它最招骂的地方。
zh.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: 终局：让「做站」这件事不再需要交接
zh.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: 如果 Agent 能读懂设计意图、CMS 能自动组织内容、托管与 SEO 默认达标，那么「设计—前端—运维」这条链上的人会被压缩成一个：改画布的人。它离这一步的距离不在模型能力，在审阅与信任机制（能不能让人放心让它改）。
zh.RISK_INTRO: 风险按「可能性 × 影响」排序；严重度是我的判断，不是官方披露。
zh.RISK_1_NAME: 账单不可预测引发的信任崩塌
zh.RISK_1_MIT: 把 credits 与附加包在动手前显式预算化；席位与语言包给打包价；取消流程做到两键。Trustpilot 的低分不是产品问题，是账单体验问题，可修。
zh.RISK_2_NAME: AI 生成站从侧翼替代
zh.RISK_2_MIT: 守「可编辑 + 托管 + 性能」三件套，并把 MCP 开放到底（让那些 agent 反而成为它的输入）；同时用导出/迁移的付费出口化解锁定争议。
zh.RISK_3_NAME: 技术 SEO 与自定义能力的天花板
zh.RISK_3_MIT: 把 robots.txt、静态文件、headers 这类能力从「附加包」提到 Pro 档默认；能力边界在页面上写清楚，比事后被差评划算。
zh.RISK_4_NAME: 支持体系跟不上付费规模
zh.RISK_4_MIT: 对一人公司与小工作室给「计费争议」专用人工通道；公开首响时长指标。这类用户单个 LTV 低，但口碑权重高。
zh.SHOT_1_CAPTION: Framer 画布视图：右侧是设计 Agent 面板，区块可直接在画布上生成与改动（来自 framer.com 首页）
zh.SHOT_2_CAPTION: 官网 Design with agents 区块：同一需求下多套设计稿的成稿预览（来自 framer.com 首页）
zh.SHOT_3_CAPTION: CMS 数据表格：内容集合以表格形式管理，Agent 可就地改写字段（来自 framer.com 首页）
zh.SHOT_4_CAPTION: 站点设置表单：SEO、域名与发布相关配置集中在同一面板（来自 framer.com 首页）
zh.SHOT_5_CAPTION: 性能指标面板：LCP / INP / CLS 等 Core Web Vitals 直接摆在产品里（来自 framer.com 首页）
zh.SHOT_6_CAPTION: 分析仪表盘：上线后的流量与页面表现（来自 framer.com 首页）
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: 设计 Agent：官网原话 a professional design agent, native to the canvas——它直接在站点上生成与修改，改动可见、可编辑、可撤销。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: CMS / Code Agent：整理集合、生成组件代码与交互，把「内容维护」也交给代理。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: [推断] MCP 外接是走向「站点即接口」的第一步：当 Claude / Cursor / Codex 能直接改站点，Framer 变成被调用的执行层，而不只是人操作的界面。
zh.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: 两条：一是「一句话生成站」的 LLM 工具从侧翼替代（能导出源码，对要代码主权的团队更有吸引力）；二是 AI 让「建站」本身贬值——当生成变便宜，收费点只能落在托管、性能与合规上，而这三处正是它已经在收的地方。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: （我的判断）把 Agent 的改动做成 diff 清单 + 一键回滚：让人敢放手让它改，这是它把「AI 生成」变成「AI 可信」的唯一路径。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: （我的判断）把「示例 → brief → 生成」做成标准三步：实测（燃冰）指出门槛在审美判断，产品接住这一步，非设计师才真正进得来。
zh.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: 已知（可在来源中逐条核对）：官网功能与模块原文、定价页四档与附加包金额（港币区域价）、Free 档细则、超额与退款规则、Marketplace 资源数 28,915、99.99% uptime、MCP 端点、Compare 页竞品清单、实测（燃冰）六维记录。推断（已标 [推断]）：公司历史沿革与融资、真实 ARR 与付费站点数、留存曲线、毛利结构、竞品金额。外部评论（G2 4.5 / Trustpilot 约 1.6 等）为第三方评测站点转述，非本报告直接抓取，引用处已标明。
zh.ASSUMPTION_1: [推断] 金额口径：本次定价页按访问地返回港币（HK$），未取到美元价；第三方评测普遍写 Basic $10/月、Pro $30/月、编辑器 $20/月、Advanced hosting $200/月，本报告只把它作为「量级参考」，不作为官方价。
zh.ASSUMPTION_2: [推断] 真实付费主力是「要上线的设计驱动团队」，不是「想用 AI 写文案的人」：依据是付费扳机在自定义域名、以及 Enterprise 档把 SSO/席位/uptime 当卖点。
zh.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: 它横跨两排货架：一排是专业建站（Webflow、Wix、Squarespace、WordPress），一排是 AI 生成站（Lovable、v0、Claude Code）。它站在中间偏设计的一侧——比 AI 生成类多了托管与 CMS 的厚度，比传统建站多了「描述即生成」的速度。
zh.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI 用在四处，都在画布上：① 设计 Agent（生成布局、区块、组件、文案）；② CMS Agent（建集合、整理内容）；③ Code Agent（生成组件代码与交互）；④ 本地化与图像/着色器生成（消耗 credits）。外部 agent 走 MCP 接入，发布前在画布复核。
zh.FINAL_BREAKS: 要代码主权的人、要复杂电商与超大规模 CMS 的团队、把技术 SEO（robots.txt/静态文件/headers）当硬要求的人、以及合约里写明「资产必须可迁移」的甲方。
zh.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: 有护城河，但位置很具体：不在模型，在「画布即生产环境 + 托管 + 模板市场」这三件耦合，加上一层「不给导出」的人为锁定。前三条要多年积累，最后一条只要改政策就能失去——它的护城河一半是能力，一半是合同条款。
zh.FINAL_WINS: 设计与发布的连续性、默认达标的性能与 SEO、28,915 个资源的长尾入口、MCP 带来的外接生态。四条里只有第一条是「别人抄不动」的。
zh.SIX_INTRO: 本轮按应用层六维写：不看它有多少 AI 功能，只看它在真实工作里替掉了哪一步、把哪些麻烦甩回给人。证据来自 2026-11-17 的 20 分钟实测（燃冰）+ 官网/定价页原文 + 第三方评论转述。
zh.AI_TYPE_REASON: 拔电测试：拿走 AI，Framer 仍是一个可视化建站 + 托管 + CMS 工具，站能建、能发、能改——所以判定为「嵌入」，不是「原生」。AI 负责生成布局、文案、代码片段与 CMS 整理，主链路仍是画布编辑与发布。
zh.SIX_1: 替掉的是「设计实现」这一步：原来由设计师做设计评估、再由开发实现，实测（燃冰）记录的量级是几个月；现在拿一张成品截图/设计稿在上面让 AI 换部件，几小时。成本从「设计师人力」变成「工具订阅」——这是它最硬的替换价值。
zh.SIX_2: 数据、权限、格式的脏活它自己啃：域名、托管、SSL、带宽、CMS 结构、SEO 元信息、发布流程都内置。甩回给人的只有一次，但这一次很关键——它要求「给示例、给需求」，也就是审美判断。实测（燃冰）的判断：甩回来的这部分，正是这个品类真正的门槛。
zh.SIX_3: 能直接用。实测（燃冰）原话是「能直接用」「直接支持外发，它是一站式网站生成工具」，需要改的是每个组件的细节，不是重做。
zh.SIX_4: 产品侧兜底靠撤销与历史（实测：支持 undo、有记录），Pro 档另有 Staging 与分支预览；但它不标来源、不给置信度、也不纠正错误前提（实测（燃冰）：它不处理这种事情，判断它不负责）。最终兜底是人——人工复核。
zh.SIX_5: 错得起。结构是可拆的（组件/图层级），有 undo 与历史，改坏能退回。真正不可逆的部分不在画布里：绑定的域名、对外发布的那一版、以及「没有代码导出」带来的迁移成本。
zh.SIX_6: 换得掉。官网自己列了近 20 个替代（Webflow、Wix、Squarespace、WordPress、Figma、Lovable、v0…），实测（燃冰）也确认可以回到原来的做法。但换的代价要算清：站要重建，且第三方转述普遍指出「没有导出」让迁移更贵。

en.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: It does not sell AI, it sells 'design file to live site': the canvas is the production environment, AI just shortens the path.
en.USER_SCALE: Verifiable: 28,915 resources in the Marketplace (templates, components, plugins, vectors); 99.99% uptime stated on the pricing page; customer quotes from Miro, Perplexity, Zapier, FLORA, Metalab and Cradle. Third-party aggregators relay G2 4.5 (~142 reviews) and Trustpilot around 1.6 (~127-140 reviews, 74% one-star). Framer publishes no ARR, site count or paid-user count.
en.STAGE_MATURITY: Mature. The site narrative has fully shifted to 'design agent' (three nav items tagged New: AI, Agents, External Agents), with Agents, CMS, Hosting, Analytics, SEO, AEO, Convert, Localization, Marketplace and Hire Experts all shipped. Founding year and funding are not on the captured pages, so they are not asserted here.
en.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: Per-site subscription (Free / Basic / Pro / Enterprise) + seats (editor HK$81/mo, content editor HK$41/mo) + add-ons (extra locale HK$81, Convert A/B HK$203 per 500k events, Advanced hosting HK$811). Captured amounts are the HK$ regional display; USD figures circulating in third-party reviews are not official.
en.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: It turned 'design file to live site' into a subscription; AI is only the accelerator. The moat is the editor plus hosting plus the template market. The wound is a bill that stacks per site, per seat and per credit.
en.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: As an embedded-AI product, pulling the AI out still leaves a usable website builder (confirmed in the 20-minute test: embedded). So its threshold is not the model, it is the software: SEO capability, hosting, and habits designers already have. The review record splits cleanly: G2 praises the editor, Trustpilot attacks the billing and support. Both are true.
en.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: AI is the accelerator, not the product
en.TLDR_1_BODY: The agent sits above the fold: describe it, get layouts and components, refine on canvas, publish. But the 20-minute test ends on a narrower claim: AI replaces the 'build the skeleton from zero' step, aesthetic judgement still belongs to the human. Remove the AI and the product still stands.
en.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: The threshold is software, not the model
en.TLDR_2_BODY: Verbatim from the test: the threshold is in the product's own SEO and in the habits of design users, in the software. Hosting, CMS, AEO, Core Web Vitals and uptime cannot be supplied by a model, and rivals cannot patch all of them at once.
en.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: The bill is the weakest beam
en.TLDR_3_BODY: The homepage shows no price; the pricing page stacks three layers: subscription per site, seats (HK$81/editor), add-ons (locales, A/B, Advanced hosting). Trustpilot sits near 1.6 with 74% one-star, complaining about billing and cancellation rather than design. That is the cost of a clean marketing face over a complicated invoice.
en.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: Framer is a website platform that fuses design, CMS, hosting, analytics and SEO into one line: what you design on the canvas is the page that ships, and the AI design agent generates layouts, sections and code fragments from a prompt.
en.USER_PROMISE: Official wording: 'Framer is the pro website builder with a world-class design agent', and 'Build your website with agents and make it your own on a fully editable design canvas'. In user language: no handoff to developers, design it and ship it.
en.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: Solutions lists Designers, Agencies, Marketers, Growth, Builders, Engineers, Site Teams and Founders; every customer quote comes from a design lead (Miro, Perplexity). What they want is stated in one review line: design ownership back in our hands.
en.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: You can build on Free and pay only when you connect a custom domain, which is real money for freelancers with slipping timelines. The test reaches the same conclusion: the free tier has genuine value through templates and community.
en.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: Enterprise adds SSO, SCIM, an uptime guarantee and unlimited editors; Pro Experts get free edit access to client projects. But per-site pricing stacked with per-seat charges is exactly where this segment complains loudest.
en.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: Turn a design idea (screenshot, reference site, Figma file) into a live, indexable site without a developer handoff.
en.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: Stop waiting in a queue, stop sending three emails to change one padding value, and stop looking like 'a template someone assembled'.
en.JTBD_SOCIAL: Look like a brand with a real site to the outside world; the quotes repeat 'ship updates daily' and 'no dev handoff'.
en.TRIGGER_MOMENT: A new brand site, a landing-page revamp or a launch date arrives while the design is settled and development has no slot.
en.FREQUENCY: Project-based: intense during redesigns and launches, low-frequency maintenance in between ([inferred] from pricing that meters sites and bandwidth, not conversations).
en.USAGE_CONTEXT: Browser first (a desktop app is also listed); publishing is hosted by Framer (99.99% uptime), content lives in the CMS, numbers in built-in Analytics, experiments in the Convert add-on.
en.LOOP_TRIGGER_TITLE: Design is done, dev is busy
en.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: The trigger is not 'I want AI', it is 'this step is stuck in someone else's queue'. Both the reviews and the test point at the same scene: a finished design that has to become a site.
en.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: Describe, or bring the design, then refine on canvas
en.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: Three official steps: describe what you need (the agent builds layouts and advanced components), refine on the canvas (type, components, breakpoints, effects), publish instantly (hosting, CMS, analytics, SEO and AEO are already there).
en.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: The reward is not 'generated code', it is 'connect the domain and go live'. The test judged the output directly usable, with per-component tweaks, and publishable as is.
en.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: A site is alive: campaign pages, A/B tests, locales and CMS updates keep pulling people back to the canvas. Retention comes from the assets staying here (site, CMS, analytics), not from the AI being impressive.
en.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: The high frequency lives inside 'the redesign week', not every day. That is why the model is a subscription rather than pay-per-use: per-use pricing cannot bill the maintenance tail.
en.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: What it teaches is 'you do not have to wait for a developer'. Once a team is used to design-and-ship, going back to handoff feels slow. That is the real retention, and the bill is what erodes it.
en.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: Three public paths: 28,915 Marketplace resources acting as long-tail entry points (template pages are SEO pages); a large set of compare pages (vs Webflow, Figma, Wix, Squarespace, WordPress, Lovable, v0, Claude Code and more) capturing selection intent; and customer quotes plus showcases as social proof.
en.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: From the test: taking a real design or screenshot and turning it into a page that can ship, with the AI swapping sections on request; what used to be months became hours. The aha is not 'it writes like a human', it is 'it produced something publishable'.
en.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: Weak and incidental: attribution on published sites, showcases and template authors bring organic spread, but there is no invite loop and no collaboration-driven virality. It spreads through artifacts, not through social graphs.
en.RETENTION_1: Asset lock-in: the site, CMS content and analytics all live here, and there is no code export (a complaint repeated across reviews), so migrating means rebuilding.
en.RETENTION_2: Habit lock-in: designers have trained the breakpoint, component and scroll-effect paths; switching means learning a new muscle memory (the test names user habits as the threshold).
en.RETENTION_3: Ecosystem lock-in: templates, components, plugins and the Experts marketplace keep even 'hire someone to fix it' inside the platform.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_1_NAME: Templates and showcases to search and community to trial
en.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: Each of the 28,915 Marketplace resources is a landing page; template authors build backlinks and tutorials to sell their work, so the platform gets distribution without paying for it.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_2_NAME: Compare pages intercept, migration feeds the story
en.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: [inferred] A compare page exists for nearly every rival, the standard long-tail SEO play for the 'which one' moment. Third-party reviews corroborate real migrations (one user reports moving from Webflow with no SEO loss over four months).
en.SURFACE_1_ROLE: The product itself: Pages, Layers and Assets on the left, properties on the right, breakpoints and Publish on top. The design object is the production object.
en.SURFACE_2_ROLE: Generates layouts, components, copy and even code from a prompt; the demo shows it producing a design plan before touching the page.
en.SURFACE_3_ROLE: Collections, fields and plugins wired to the canvas; Free allows 10 collections and 1,000 pages, paid tiers meter collections and items.
en.SURFACE_4_ROLE: Title, URL, description, social preview, locale coverage, branches and publishing. The technical-SEO ceiling lives on this page (reviews name robots.txt and static files).
en.SURFACE_5_ROLE: Visitors, page views, bounce rate, session length plus A/B variants and conversion; Convert is an add-on billed per event (HK$203 per 500k events).
en.SURFACE_6_ROLE: 28,915 templates, components, plugins and vectors; if you cannot build it yourself, the platform also connects you to experts.
en.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: The organising axis is the site, not the file: pick a project, then a page, then a breakpoint and a layer; CMS, analytics, SEO and locales are all sub-settings of that site. There is no knowledge-base layer; the asset is the site, which is the structural reason migration is expensive.
en.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: Near-zero learning cost for designers (a Figma-shaped canvas), a vocabulary tax for everyone else: breakpoint, collection, branch, locale, credits. The test did not get stuck on the interface, it got stuck on aesthetic judgement: the UI is not hard, the decision is.
en.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: There is no 'design, hand off, rebuild' segment: what you change on the canvas is the version that ships. That is the root of every experience advantage and every lock-in risk.
en.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: Official line: everything stays editable. What it generates is a set of layers and components, not a picture. Reviewers praise exactly this: you tweak piece by piece instead of redrawing.
en.CRAFT_3_NAME: SEO, AEO and performance as defaults
en.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: The homepage displays a live Core Web Vitals panel (LCP 1.1s, INP 95ms, CLS 0.01), and the company ships its own AEO scanner and Stack Score. The pitch is not 'you can optimise', it is 'it is already fine'.
en.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: Credits fuel agents and localization and are shared across the workspace; running low means upgrading a site or buying an add-on. It monetises heavy use continuously, and it makes the invoice hard to predict, which is where Trustpilot complaints come from.
en.CRAFT_5_NAME: Compare pages that mop up selection traffic
en.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: The Compare menu lists close to twenty rivals (Webflow, Figma, Wix, Squarespace, WordPress, Lovable, v0, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Replit, Astro and more). Each page answers one question: why not them.
en.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: First make designers want to stay inside it, then talk about how much AI can generate. Every AI feature lives on the canvas rather than in a separate chat window, and that is the real difference from prompt-to-site tools.
en.TTV_LABEL: Time to value: not measured this round (the test recorded 'hours for one page rebuild', not a stopwatch figure)
en.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: The test records an order of magnitude, not seconds: months became hours. This report does not convert that into a precise number.
en.COG_LABEL: Cognitive load: medium (low for designers, medium-high for others; vocabulary tax on breakpoint / collection / locale / credits)
en.DELIGHT_1: Everything generated stays editable (official line, and the test changed per-component details rather than rebuilding).
en.DELIGHT_2: MCP is open: Claude, Codex and Cursor can connect to edit copy and import CMS content (endpoint mcp.framer.com/mcp).
en.DELIGHT_3: A performance panel sits on the homepage: LCP 1.1s, INP 95ms, CLS 0.01, making speed a fact rather than an adjective.
en.DELIGHT_LABEL: Delight: editable generation, MCP access, default performance
en.TRUST_LABEL: Trust: the product side offers 99.99% uptime plus SSO/SCIM on Enterprise; trust incidents cluster on billing (credits, seats, add-ons) and support responsiveness.
en.STRUGGLE_1: Unpredictable billing: subscription plus seats plus credits plus add-ons. Relayed Trustpilot complaints centre on upgrades and add-ons exceeding expectations.
en.STRUGGLE_2: No code export, so leaving means rebuilding: relayed review line, impossible to leave Framer without export and they do not provide it.
en.STRUGGLE_3: A technical-SEO ceiling: relayed reports of no robots.txt editing, and static file uploads locked behind the Advanced hosting add-on.
en.STRUGGLE_LABEL: Friction: unpredictable billing, no export, technical-SEO limits
en.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Four tiers: Free (500 credits, Framer subdomain, 1 GB bandwidth); Basic (1,000-15,000 credits, custom domain, 2 CMS collections, 50 GB); Pro (3,000-100,000 credits, 10 collections, 100 GB, redirects, staging, branching with previews, with A/B and Advanced hosting as add-ons); Enterprise (custom credits, SSO, SCIM, unlimited editors, uptime guarantee). Refunds: 14 days for EU and Turkey.
en.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: Free lets you build and preview, but the pricing page states a custom domain requires an upgrade. The paywall is not 'AI ran out', it is 'you want to ship', which is a much better-placed trigger.
en.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: Free: 500 AI credits per month, Framer subdomain, 1 GB bandwidth, 10 CMS collections, 1,000 pages, 5 MB uploads, one free locale, up to three editors; no custom domain. Overages: bandwidth can exceed the limit for one month with an email notice; credits can be topped up or a site upgraded.
en.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: Locally aligned, structurally in tension. Aligned: the paywall (domain) is exactly the value moment (going live), so nobody feels gated before value. In tension: credits and seats charge for more use while the experience goal is to keep you editing, so the more you iterate the less predictable the bill, and that is the crack in trust scores.
en.COMP_1_D2: Own visual CSS engine plus hosting, stronger export and code control
en.COMP_1_D4: Public pricing page; amounts not individually verified here
en.COMP_2_D1: General website building (same need, different buyer)
en.COMP_2_D2: Templates, drag and drop, full hosting; AI site generation as an add-on
en.COMP_2_D4: Public pricing pages; amounts not individually verified
en.COMP_3_D1: The direct exit for design files
en.COMP_3_D2: Publishes from inside the design tool, removing the import step
en.COMP_3_D3: Default position inside existing design teams
en.COMP_3_D4: Bundled with Figma plans; not verified
en.COMP_4_D2: LLM-generated React/Tailwind deployed elsewhere, source exportable
en.COMP_OWN_D1: Design-to-live professional building with bundled hosting
en.COMP_OWN_D2: Canvas as production, editable AI output, CMS/analytics/SEO/AEO built in
en.COMP_OWN_D3: Designer community, 28,915-resource marketplace, compare-page SEO, MCP access
en.COMP_OWN_D4: No price on the homepage; four tiers plus three add-on layers on the pricing page
en.COMP_INTRO: Names come from Framer's own Compare pages (Webflow, Figma, Wix, Squarespace, WordPress, Readymag, Ceros, Unbounce, Lovable, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, Contentful, Sanity, AEM, Replit, Astro, v0) plus destinations users name in third-party reviews. Product Hunt's Similar Products block was not captured (Cloudflare block), which is stated rather than guessed.
en.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: Continuity between design and publishing: think, build and ship on one canvas, with generated output editable object by object. Reviewers keep praising breakpoint work and the cost of motion, which prompt-to-code tools cannot reproduce yet.
en.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: Three ways: teams that want code ownership leave for LLM builders (Lovable, v0, Claude Code) because the source is exportable; content-heavy and commerce complexity tops out below Webflow and Shopify (CMS caps, no native commerce); and the cheap edge is eaten by Wix, Squarespace and open-source stacks.
en.CHANNEL_1: Template and showcase ecosystem: 28,915 Marketplace resources as long-tail entry points.
en.CHANNEL_2: Selection-intent compare pages: close to twenty rival comparisons under one menu.
en.CHANNEL_3: Customer quotes plus the Experts marketplace: design leads at Miro, Perplexity and Zapier, with services kept inside the ecosystem.
en.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: Subscription plus seats (HK$81/editor) plus credits plus add-ons (locale HK$81, Convert HK$203 per 500k events, Advanced hosting HK$811). Relayed Trustpilot complaints (near 1.6, 74% one-star) centre on upgrades and add-ons costing more than expected. Users are not refusing to pay; they cannot compute the price in advance.
en.FRICTION_2_TITLE: No export, so leaving means rebuilding
en.FRICTION_2_BODY: Relayed review line: impossible to leave Framer without export and they do not provide it; the r/framer consensus is that lock-in and lack of code export are the trade-offs for that simplicity. It is a business choice and a trust cost at once.
en.FRICTION_3_BODY: Relayed reports: no robots.txt editing, and static uploads (up to 500 files) sit behind the Advanced hosting add-on at HK$811. Built-in SEO and the AEO scanner are real for metadata and markup, but anything deeper should be checked before committing a site.
en.FRICTION_4_TITLE: Support is the second complaint line
en.FRICTION_4_BODY: Relayed reports: bot-first support, slow replies, a Trustpilot flag for not replying to negative reviews, and Capterra's ease-of-use sub-score at the bottom of its range. That hurts solopreneurs most, because when it breaks there is nobody to ask.
en.METRICS_INTRO: No operating metrics are public. What follows is verifiable fact plus [inferred] reasoning about what it should watch, not real data.
en.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: Published sites multiplied by monthly maintenance actions per site ([inferred])
en.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [inferred] It bills per site and monetises seats and credits: site count is the revenue base and 'still being edited' is the precondition for renewal and upsell. So the number that matters is live, maintained sites, not signups.
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: Connecting a domain is the only paywall (pricing page states it requires an upgrade), so this number decides whether the free tier is a cost or a funnel.
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: Credits consumed per site and add-on purchase rate
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: Credits meter the AI features and are the source of billing disputes; a high top-up rate proves the AI is working, and predicts that complaints will rise with it.
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: Seats are the second growth curve and the easiest line to resent (HK$81 per editor); it decides whether the team edition holds up.
en.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: Billing and refund complaints plus first-response time
en.GUARDRAIL_WHY: Trustpilot near 1.6 alongside G2 at 4.5 means product satisfaction is not commercial satisfaction. These two are the only guardrails that separate design reputation from billing reputation.
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: No public retention curve, migration rate or gross margin, and no per-site cost of bandwidth or inference [inferred]
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [inferred] It sells subscriptions and pays for bandwidth and inference: watching revenue without unit cost hides a margin that gets worse as it grows. Meanwhile 'no export' pushes migration down and complaints up, and neither direction is disclosed.
en.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: Editor feel 7, hosting/CMS/SEO integration 7, template ecosystem 7, migration lock-in 8, price and support 4, AI capability 5, weighted 6: the AI can be copied, the 'design is production' coupling cannot.
en.HORIZONTAL_1: From building to operating: Analytics, Convert (A/B, funnels), Localization, SEO/AEO scanner, capturing the life after launch.
en.HORIZONTAL_2: [inferred] From designers to marketers and founders: Solutions now splits Designers, Marketers, Founders, Agencies, shifting the story from design tool to growth tool.
en.VERTICAL_1: Professional and brand sites: portfolios, landing pages, marketing sites, agency client work (Pro Experts get free edit access to client projects).
en.VERTICAL_2: CMS-driven content sites: blog, cases, campaign pages; the ceiling is collections and items (up to 40 collections and 40,000 items with Pro add-ons).
en.PLATFORM_1: An open interface exists: the MCP endpoint mcp.framer.com/mcp lets external agents (Claude, Codex, Cursor) edit site content, reviewed on the canvas before publishing.
en.PLATFORM_2: [inferred] Platform strategy runs on protocol plus marketplace: no transaction take rate, but MCP turns outside agents into free labour and the Marketplace turns template authors into free distribution.
en.OPP_1_HEADLINE: (my judgement) Make 'changed and shipped' a reviewable diff
en.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: How: after every agent pass, list which layers, components and copy changed, with one-click rollback to the previous version. Why: the test says the work is per-component tweaking, and reviewing is what lets a person dare to delegate; it is also the only trust gap against prompt-to-site rivals.
en.OPP_2_HEADLINE: (my judgement) Turn example-driven prompting into a built-in reference library
en.OPP_2_DETAIL: How: have the agent ask for a reference example on the first turn and write the ask into a structured brief the human confirms before it builds. Why: the test records 'it required me to find an example and give requirements', which is precisely the aesthetic threshold; catching that step is how non-designers get in.
en.OPP_3_HEADLINE: (my judgement) Quote the bill before work starts
en.OPP_3_DETAIL: How: show the credits a redesign will consume and which add-ons it touches (locales, A/B, hosting) before anything runs, with a warning before the limit. Why: the Trustpilot score is driven by unpredictable billing, and this fix needs no architecture change, making it the lightest lever.
en.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: The bet: use AI to lower 'zero to shippable', use hosting and ecosystem to keep the site
en.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: Two bets at once: put agents inside the canvas (design, CMS, code) so non-designers can start, and keep pulling post-launch work (hosting, analytics, A/B, locales, AEO) into the subscription. The first widens the audience, the second lifts ARPU, and 'no export' is the licence to do both, which is also why it draws the loudest complaints.
en.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: Endgame: making a website stop requiring a handoff
en.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: If agents read design intent, the CMS organises content and hosting plus SEO are compliant by default, the chain of designer, front-end and ops collapses into one person editing a canvas. The distance is not model capability, it is review and trust: can a person let it change things without watching.
en.RISK_INTRO: Risks are ordered by likelihood times impact; severity is my judgement, not a company disclosure.
en.RISK_1_MIT: Quote credits and add-ons before work starts, bundle seats and locales, make cancellation two clicks. The low Trustpilot score is a billing-experience problem, and it is fixable.
en.RISK_2_MIT: Defend editable plus hosting plus performance, open MCP all the way so rival agents become inputs, and defuse the lock-in argument with a paid export or migration path.
en.RISK_3_MIT: Move robots.txt, static files and headers from add-on to Pro default, and state the capability boundary on the page; that is cheaper than a one-star review.
en.RISK_4_NAME: Support not scaling with paying users
en.RISK_4_MIT: Give solopreneurs and small studios a human billing-dispute lane and publish first-response times; their LTV is low but their word-of-mouth weight is high.
en.SHOT_1_CAPTION: Framer canvas with the design agent panel: sections are generated and edited directly on the canvas (from framer.com home)
en.SHOT_2_CAPTION: The 'Design with agents' block on the official site: finished design variations for the same brief (from framer.com home)
en.SHOT_3_CAPTION: CMS table view: content collections managed as a table, fields editable in place with agents (from framer.com home)
en.SHOT_4_CAPTION: Site settings form: SEO, domain and publishing options in one panel (from framer.com home)
en.SHOT_5_CAPTION: Performance panel: Core Web Vitals such as LCP / INP / CLS shown inside the product (from framer.com home)
en.SHOT_6_CAPTION: Analytics dashboard: post-launch traffic and page performance (from framer.com home)
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Design agent: official wording, a professional design agent native to the canvas, generating and refining in place with every change visible, editable and under control.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: CMS and code agents: organising collections and generating component code and interactions, handing content maintenance over too.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: [inferred] MCP is the first step toward site-as-interface: once Claude, Cursor or Codex can edit the site directly, Framer becomes the execution layer that gets called, not only an interface a human drives.
en.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: Two: prompt-to-site LLM tools flank it with exportable source for teams that want code ownership; and AI deflates building itself, so the chargeable value shifts to hosting, performance and compliance, which is exactly where it already charges.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: (my judgement) Turn agent edits into a diff list with one-click rollback: that is how 'AI generates' becomes 'AI is trusted'.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: (my judgement) Standardise example, brief, then build: the test shows the threshold is aesthetic judgement, and catching that step is how non-designers actually enter.
en.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: Known and checkable in the sources: official feature and module copy, four pricing tiers and add-on amounts (HK$ regional display), free-tier details, overage and refund rules, 28,915 Marketplace resources, 99.99% uptime, the MCP endpoint, the Compare rival list, and the six-dimension test record. Inferred and labelled: company history and funding, real ARR and paid site count, retention curve, margin structure, rival pricing. External review scores (G2 4.5, Trustpilot near 1.6) are relayed by third-party review sites and were not scraped directly, which is stated at each use.
en.ASSUMPTION_1: [inferred] Currency: the pricing page returned HK$ for this session and no USD figure was captured; third-party reviews commonly cite Basic $10/mo, Pro $30/mo, editor $20/mo, Advanced hosting $200/mo. Those are treated as order-of-magnitude references, not official prices.
en.ASSUMPTION_2: [inferred] The paying core is design-driven teams that need to ship, not people who want AI copy: the paywall sits on the custom domain and Enterprise sells SSO, seats and uptime.
en.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: It straddles two shelves: professional builders (Webflow, Wix, Squarespace, WordPress) and AI site generators (Lovable, v0, Claude Code). It stands on the design side of the middle: thicker than prompt-to-site tools on hosting and CMS, faster than classic builders thanks to describe-and-generate.
en.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI appears in four places, all on the canvas: the design agent (layouts, sections, components, copy), the CMS agent (collections and content), the code agent (component code and interactions), and localization plus image/shader generation (credit-metered). External agents connect over MCP and changes are reviewed on the canvas before publishing.
en.FINAL_BREAKS: Teams that need code ownership, complex commerce or very large CMS estates, teams that treat robots.txt, static files and headers as hard requirements, and clients whose contracts demand portable assets.
en.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: A moat exists, but its location is specific: not the model, but the coupling of canvas-as-production, hosting and the template market, plus an artificial lock from having no export. The first three take years to build; the last can be lost with one policy change. Half of the moat is capability and half is contract terms.
en.FINAL_WINS: Continuity between design and publishing, default-compliant performance and SEO, the 28,915-resource long-tail funnel, and the MCP access layer. Only the first is something rivals cannot copy quickly.
en.SIX_INTRO: Written against the six application-layer dimensions: not how many AI features it has, but which step it removes and which messes it hands back. Evidence: the 20-minute test on 2026-11-17, official site and pricing pages, and relayed third-party reviews.
en.AI_TYPE_REASON: Unplug test: remove the AI and Framer is still a visual website builder with hosting and CMS. Sites can be built, shipped and edited, so the type is embedded, not AI-native. Agents generate layouts, copy, code and CMS structure; the main path remains canvas editing and publishing.
en.SIX_1: It removes the design-implementation step: designers used to do the design assessment and developers implemented it, which the test records as months; now you bring a finished screenshot or design and swap sections with the agent, which takes hours. Cost moves from designer labour to a tool subscription, and that is the hardest value it replaces.
en.SIX_2: The unglamorous work is handled: domains, hosting, SSL, bandwidth, CMS structure, SEO metadata and publishing are built in. It hands back exactly one thing, but a decisive one: it asks for an example and for requirements, which is aesthetic judgement. The test concludes that handed-back part is the real threshold of this category.
en.SIX_3: Directly usable. The test records 'usable as is', 'supports publishing externally, it is an all-in-one site generator', and says the changes needed are per-component detail rather than a rebuild.
en.SIX_4: Product-side safety is undo and history (the test confirms both), plus staging and branch previews on Pro. But it does not cite sources, does not give confidence and does not correct a false premise (the test: it does not handle that, judgement is not its job). The final safety net is a human review.
en.SIX_5: Mistakes are affordable. The structure is decomposable at component and layer level, undo and history exist. What is not reversible sits outside the canvas: a connected domain, a published version, and the migration cost created by the absence of code export.
en.SIX_6: Reversible. Framer's own site lists close to twenty alternatives (Webflow, Wix, Squarespace, WordPress, Figma, Lovable, v0 and more), and the test confirms a return to the old way is possible. The price is rebuilding the site, and relayed reviews agree the missing export makes migration expensive.

谁抢同一个需求抢同一段链路用户实际迁移
Webflow设计师做专业站画布 + 托管 + CMS双向流动：设计师选 Framer 求手感，要代码控制的人回 Webflow（第三方转述的设计师/开发者分野）
Wix / Squarespace非设计师想上线模板 + 拖拽 + 托管价格敏感段被它们接走（评论点名低价替代）
Figma Sites设计稿想直接发设计文件到站点这一段[推断] 已在 Figma 里的团队最省事，抢的是「导入」这一步
Lovable / v0 / Claude Code一句话生成站生成与代码要源码与自由部署的人往这边走（评论原话点名没有导出是离开的原因）
WordPress内容站与自主可控CMS + SEO + 插件技术 SEO 受限的人（robots.txt / 静态文件）往回走
Readymag / Ceros / Unbounce营销页与互动页单页制作与投放[推断] 单一场景被更专的工具切走，官网把它们的对比页都建了

结论：抢同一段链路的是 Webflow 与 Figma Sites（画布到上线），抢同一个需求的是 Wix 与 AI 生成类。真正让用户离开的不是功能短板，是账单与导出——这两条都不在功能对比表里。

extra_zh.title: 竞品技术底座
extra_zh.body:
看底座比看功能快：底座决定了它「不做什么」，也就决定了它会输在哪。

产品技术底座（公开可核实）锁住了什么能力
Framer自研画布编辑器 + 自建托管与 CDN + 内置 CMS / 分析 / 本地化；MCP 对外开放（mcp.framer.com/mcp）「设计即生产」的连续感、默认达标的 Core Web Vitals（LCP 1.1s / INP 95ms / CLS 0.01）、以及不给导出的锁定
Webflow自研可视化 CSS 引擎 + 托管 + 更强的代码导出与自定义代码位对 CSS 与结构的精确控制；代价是学习曲线
Wix / Squarespace模板系统 + 拖拽 + 全托管，AI 建站为附加层上手速度与价格带，锁在低复杂度站点
WordPressPHP + MySQL + 插件生态，自托管资产主权与无限扩展；代价是运维
Lovable / v0 / Claude CodeLLM 生成 React / Tailwind 代码，部署在第三方平台，源码可导出代码主权与自由部署，锁不住用户

哪一层是真护城河[推断]：不在模型层——Framer 用的模型能力是外部可得的；在「画布 + 托管 + CMS + 模板市场」的耦合。这一层难在多年打磨与生态，不在算法；而「没有导出」是一层人造锁定，改政策就能失去，所以它既是护城河也是风险源。

extra_zh.title: 可迁移的机会
extra_zh.body:
写给一人公司和小团队，四条能直接用。每条先问一句：这个弱点换个渠道还是不是弱点？

一、把「示例 + 需求」做成开工前的 brief（我的判断）。Framer 的 Agent 要人先给示例，实测（燃冰）就卡在这一步。换个场景照样成立：任何「生成型」工具，把用户脑子里的参考物先结构化成 brief，就能把审美判断这道门槛降下来。最轻：一个三步表单 + 一次确认。

二、把改动做成 diff（我的判断）。它支持 undo，但不告诉人「这次动了什么」。做内容或代码类 AI 产品，改动清单 + 一键回滚是通用刚需——因为它同时解决审阅与定价争议两个问题。

三、账单前置（我的判断）。Framer 的 Trustpilot 低分几乎全是「没想到这么贵」。任何按量计费的产品，把预估账单放在动手前，是最便宜的信任投资；这条换到 API、算力、投放任何渠道都成立。

四、把「迁移出口」做成产品（我的判断）。「不能导出」是它最招骂的地方，也是别人不敢做的位置：谁能把「进来容易、出去也容易」讲清楚，谁就能在同一个需求里收「信任溢价」。最轻的做法：一键导出结构化内容 + 站点快照。

extra_zh.title: 流量与变现拆解
extra_zh.body:
套利三问。① 钱从谁的兜里出：设计驱动的市场团队与代理商（按站点订阅）、团队里的每个编辑（按席位）、重度用 AI 的人（按 credits）、要多语言与实验的人（按附加包）。② 还能拿多久：只要「设计即上线」的手感没被 AI 生成类追平，就能继续拿；一旦能导出源码的工具把画布体验补齐，议价权会掉。③ 凭什么你拿到：28,915 个模板与组件构成的长尾入口 + 近 20 个对比页接住的选型流量 + 客户证言（Miro / Perplexity / Zapier）——三条都不是产品功能，是分发资产。

流量吃爆款还是长尾。两样都吃，但偏长尾：模板页、作品页、对比页都是典型的长尾结构；爆款来自产品发布与设计社区的作品展示。[推断] 官网把 Compare 做成近 20 个独立页面，说明它自己算过「选型词」的转化比通用词高。

变现三层结构。第一层订阅（按站点，决定收入底座）→ 第二层席位（按编辑人头，决定团队扩张的弹性）→ 第三层附加包（语言、A/B、Advanced hosting，决定重度用户的榨取率）。定价页把三层写得清楚，首页一个价格都不放——这是刻意把价格推到「已决定要上线」的那一刻。

最脆的那根梁。不是 AI 能力，是「免费档先建、绑域名才付」与「credits/席位/附加包三层计量」之间的落差：入口体验干净，出口账单复杂。Trustpilot 约 1.6 分、74% 一星，几乎全部砸在这一点上。[推断] 这条梁不修，它的 ARPU 会继续涨、口碑会继续掉，最后靠企业档与代理商计划兜住——那是另一门生意。

extra_en.title: Competitive map
extra_en.body:
A missing piece first: Product Hunt's Similar Products block was not captured (Cloudflare). The names below come from Framer's own Compare pages plus destinations users name in third-party reviews.

WhoSame needSame link in the chainActual migration
WebflowDesigners building professional sitesCanvas, hosting, CMSTwo-way: designers pick Framer for feel, teams needing code control return to Webflow
Wix / SquarespaceNon-designers who need to shipTemplates, drag and drop, hostingThey own the price-sensitive edge
Figma SitesDesign files that should publishDesign file to live site[inferred] cheapest for teams already in Figma; it removes the import step
Lovable / v0 / Claude CodePrompt-to-siteGeneration and codeTeams wanting source and free deployment go here; reviews name the missing export as the reason
WordPressContent sites with ownershipCMS, SEO, pluginsUsers blocked by technical-SEO limits move back
Readymag / Ceros / UnbounceMarketing and interactive pagesSingle-page production and campaigns[inferred] narrow scenarios go to narrower tools; Framer built compare pages for all of them

Reading: Webflow and Figma Sites compete for the same chain (canvas to publish); Wix and AI generators compete for the same need. What actually pushes users out is not a missing feature but billing and export, and neither appears on a feature comparison table.

extra_en.title: Rivals' technical base
extra_en.body:
Reading the base is faster than reading features: the base decides what a product will not do, and therefore where it loses.

ProductBase (publicly verifiable)What it locks in
FramerOwn canvas editor, own hosting and CDN, built-in CMS, analytics and localization; open MCP endpointThe continuity of design-as-production, default Core Web Vitals, and a lock created by having no export
WebflowOwn visual CSS engine, hosting, stronger code export and custom code slotsPrecise CSS and structural control, at the cost of a learning curve
Wix / SquarespaceTemplate systems, drag and drop, full hosting, AI generation as an add-onSpeed to start and price band, capped at low-complexity sites
WordPressPHP, MySQL, plugin ecosystem, self-hostedAsset ownership and unbounded extension, at the cost of operations
Lovable / v0 / Claude CodeLLM-generated React/Tailwind deployed elsewhere, source exportableCode ownership and free deployment; it cannot lock anyone in

Where the real moat is [inferred]: not the model layer, since the underlying capability is externally available; it is the coupling of canvas, hosting, CMS and template market. That layer is hard because of years of polishing and ecosystem, not algorithms. No export is an artificial lock that a policy change could remove, which makes it both a moat and a risk.

extra_en.title: Transferable opportunities
extra_en.body:
Written for one-person companies and small teams, four that can be used directly. Before each, ask whether the weakness survives a change of channel.

1. Turn example plus requirement into a brief (my judgement). Framer's agent asks for a reference example, and the test stalled exactly there. Any generative tool has the same shape: structuring the reference in the user's head into a brief lowers the aesthetic threshold. Lightest version: a three-step form and one confirmation.

2. Make edits a diff (my judgement). It supports undo but never says what changed. For any content or code AI product, a change list plus one-click rollback is universal: it solves review and billing disputes at once.

3. Quote the bill up front (my judgement). Almost every low Trustpilot score says "I did not expect that price". Putting an estimate before the action is the cheapest trust investment in any metered product, whether API, compute or ads.

4. Make the exit a product (my judgement). "No export" is its loudest complaint and a position rivals avoid: whoever can say "easy in, easy out" can charge a trust premium in the same need. Lightest version: one-click structured content export plus a site snapshot.

extra_en.title: Traffic and monetisation
extra_en.body:
The three arbitrage questions. 1. Whose pocket: design-driven marketing teams and agencies (per site), every editor on the team (seats), heavy AI users (credits), multi-locale and experiment teams (add-ons). 2. For how long: as long as the design-to-live feel is not matched by prompt-to-code tools; once those tools close the canvas gap, pricing power drops. 3. Why you get it: 28,915 template and component long-tail pages, close to twenty compare pages capturing selection intent, and customer quotes from Miro, Perplexity and Zapier. None of the three is a feature; they are distribution assets.

Hits or long tail. Both, skewed long tail: template pages, showcases and compare pages are long-tail structures, while hits come from launches and design-community showcases. [inferred] Building close to twenty compare pages suggests selection keywords convert better than generic ones.

Three monetisation layers. Subscription per site (revenue base), seats per editor (elasticity of team growth), add-ons for locales, A/B and Advanced hosting (extraction from heavy users). The pricing page spells out all three while the homepage shows no price at all, deliberately postponing price until the moment the decision to ship is made.

The weakest beam. Not AI capability but the gap between "build free, pay when you connect a domain" and the three-layer metering of credits, seats and add-ons: clean entrance, complicated exit. Trustpilot near 1.6 with 74% one-star lands almost entirely there. [inferred] Left unfixed, ARPU keeps rising while reputation falls, and the balance is held up by enterprise and agency programmes, which is a different business.
